The Journey

How I got here

Three years, a design degree, two international awards, and a habit of not stopping at the Figma file. Click a year.

'21
Communication Design, Akademia Evolucion Where the obsession with type and hierarchy started.
Started a BA in Communication Design in Prishtina: visual communication, branding, typography, UI/UX, product design and multimedia. Three years of learning why things work before learning to make them look good. That order turned out to matter.
TypographyBrandingFoundations
'24
FormBrand, and an award I didn't expect The RrugeFest identity picked up two international recognitions.
Joined FormBrand as Visual & UI/UX Designer, designing interfaces for campaigns and merchandise, and building brand systems. The RrugeFest festival identity, built on adaptive typography, high-contrast colour and the theme "Infused Void", earned an Honorable Mention at the IDA Design Awards and recognition from the World Brand Design Society. First time outside opinion confirmed what I was doing.
Brand IdentityCampaignIDA Award
'25
Started teaching at Cacttus Education Explaining the craft made me much better at it.
Became Visual/UI Design Trainer at Cacttus Education, teaching practical design workflows: UI, visual hierarchy, typography, layout and core principles. Nothing exposes a shaky opinion faster than a room of students asking why. Teaching forced me to turn instinct into reasoning I could defend.
TeachingUI DesignTypography
'25
Freelance, and full ownership Two Netherlands brands, end to end.
Two projects that covered everything. For DutchDrops, a Netherlands e-commerce agency, I led the full site redesign and reworked their brand book alongside it. For Tre Plus, a nearshore engineering company, I built the brand from nothing: logo, identity system, brand book and the entire website. Owning both halves changed how I design each one.
Brand IdentityWeb DesignE-commerceUI/UX
'26
Agilyti, and shipping my own work Stopped handing off. Started building.
Joined Agilyti, an American AI and data engineering company, in April 2026, designing across the full company surface: website, product sections, brand assets, campaigns and editorial. This is where I stopped stopping at the Figma file. Using AI tooling, I take sections from concept to production HTML myself, so what I design is what deploys. Same design instinct, far shorter distance between idea and live.
ProductDesign SystemMotionWeb

What You Get

First frame to final pixel

I care about typography, spacing, hierarchy and consistency more than decoration. My default is to remove what isn't working.

01

Product & UI Design

Interfaces built around real problems: research-informed flows, wireframes and high-fidelity UI that survives production.

02

Design Systems

Tokens, components and rules that keep a product consistent as it grows, and make handoff effortless.

03

Web & Landing Pages

Responsive sites and landing pages designed for hierarchy and conversion, not just aesthetics.

04

Brand & Identity

Award-recognised identity work: logo systems, typography, colour, and the brand books that hold it together.

05

Motion & Interaction

Scroll choreography, transitions and interactive detail. Animation that explains something.

06

Design → Live

I build what I design. Using AI tooling I take a concept to production HTML and put it live, with no handoff round and no waiting on a developer.
